title: CoderHelm plugin manifest
description: The plugin.yaml file at the root of a plugin folder (also read as plugin.yml or .coderhelm/plugin.yaml). A plugin is text plus approved tools: its behavior comes from its agents and skills, and this file declares what it may touch. Unknown fields are refused.

$schema.description: Optional. Point editors at this schema for completion and checks.

name.description: The plugin's name: lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`, at most 40 characters. With a `namespace`, the plugin's id is `namespace-name`.

namespace.description: Optional publisher name, so two sources can each have a `marketing` plugin. The id becomes `namespace-name`.

version.description: The plugin's version, as `1.2` or `1.2.0`. Installs are pinned by content hash, so the version is a label for people; raise it whenever you publish.

description.description: What the plugin does, in a sentence or two. Shown in the catalog and on the plugin's page.

skills.description: Globs of the plugin's skills, relative to the plugin's folder. Skills use the same SKILL.md format as skill repos and apply only to this plugin's runs.

agents.description: Globs of the plugin's agents. Each agent file is Markdown with frontmatter; its body is the agent's instructions.

commands.description: Globs of the plugin's commands: Markdown steps an agent can follow.

settings.description: Values each team fills in on the plugin's page. Values live with the team, never in the plugin.

tools.description: Every tool the plugin's agents may call. A tool that is not listed here does not exist for a plugin run. Every run also has `read_plugin_skill` and `save_draft` without asking.

triggers.description: What starts a run of the plugin.

outputs.description: What a run produces. Drafts wait in the review queue; a publish output sends an approved draft out through a consequential tool.

budget.description: The plugin's own monthly token limit. The team can change it on the plugin's page, and the team's limits apply too.

monthly_tokens.description: Tokens the plugin may use per month. 0 means no limit of its own.

mdGlob.description: A relative path or glob ending in `.md`, with no `..`.

key.description: The setting's name: lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`.

type.description: `string` is a value the team types. `secret` is sealed, never shown again once saved, and never given to a model. `connection` asks the team to connect an account.

provider.description: For a `connection`: how it signs in, such as `oauth2`, `mcp` or `key`.

scopes.description: For a connection: the scopes asked for. Adding a scope in a new version waits for an admin.

sensitive.description: Never shown again once saved, and never given to a model.

description.description: What the team should enter, shown on the plugin's page.

risk.description: `read` only looks. `write` changes something a person can still review, such as a draft in a CMS or an image. `consequential` reaches people or money (publish, send, post) and runs only after a person approves the exact version. A declared risk can raise a tool's risk, never lower it below what CoderHelm works out from the tool's name and method.

mcpTool.description: Tools from an MCP server the team has on its Connections page.

allow.description: Tool names, or narrow patterns such as `get_*`, the plugin may call. Never `*`: a plugin never gets every tool of a server.

description.description: When an agent should use these tools.

httpTool.description: A tool the plugin defines that calls an outside service over HTTPS with the team's connection. The token comes from the connection; the manifest never carries credentials.

name.description: Lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`. Agents call the tool by this name.

connection.description: The key of a `connection` setting whose token is sent.

method.description: Anything but GET changes something, so it is at least `write`.

description.description: When an agent should use the tool.

headers.description: Extra request headers, such as an API version. Never credentials: Authorization, Cookie, Host, Content-Length, Transfer-Encoding and Proxy-* are refused.

body.description: The JSON body to send. Strings may use `{{title}}`, `{{content}}`, `{{kind}}`, `{{channel}}` and `{{setting:<key>}}` (a string setting that isn't sensitive); values are inserted as text, so they can never add keys. Without it the body is `{title, content, kind, channel}`.

builtinTool.description: One of CoderHelm's own read-only tools, such as reading release notes. A plugin can't add a built-in that writes.

description.description: When an agent should use the tool.

manualTrigger.description: A person starts a run from the plugin's page by filling in a short form.

form.description: The form's fields: `text` for a box to write in, or a list of choices to pick from. At most 10 fields.

agent.description: The agent (its file's name, without `.md`) that answers this trigger. The first agent when unset.

cron.description: Five-field cron in UTC: minute, hour, day of month, month, day of week.

agent.description: The agent (its file's name, without `.md`) that answers this trigger. The first agent when unset.

releaseTrigger.description: Runs when CoderHelm writes release notes for a new release tag. The run gets those notes.

repos.description: Only releases of these repositories (`owner/name`). Every repository when unset.

agent.description: The agent (its file's name, without `.md`) that answers this trigger. The first agent when unset.

kinds.description: The kinds of draft a run may save.

via.description: The name of a `consequential` tool from `tools` that sends an approved draft out.

role.description: A label for the approver group, such as `marketing_editor`. The team lists the actual approvers on the plugin's page.

min.description: How many different people must approve.

approval.description: The approval a draft needs before it is published. The person who asked for a draft never approves it.

results.description: Reading a published item's numbers back after a while, as a lesson the plugin's next runs read.

tool.description: A read-only tool on that server, such as `query_insight`.

after_days.description: Days after publishing to read the results.
